To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified two antigenic changes in bladder epithelia which are early events in the development of bladder cancer, and we are using these markers for the detection of tumor recurrence and the monitoring of chemopreventure measures.
the antigenic and molecular markers we have identified are useful in monitoring the efficacy of chemotherapeutic measures.

1) the expression of the M344 mucin antigen and the 19A211 surface antigen are associated with early and superficial bladder tumors and can be used for monitoring tumor recurrence in previously treated but tumor‐free patients, 2) the expression of T138 and TCSF are associated with high grade and invasive tumors, and 3) the presence of HPV 16 sequences is inversely related to the presence of p 53 mutations in bladder tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new strategies of chemopreventions based on the detection and characterization of early lesions and premalignant changes in bladder tumors and on the identification of molecular events associated with their malignant progression.
the development of new tools for the early detection and prevention of bladder cancers.
the identification of tumor antigens expressed on premalignant and malignant cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no conclusive evidence that any chemopreventative agent can prevent the development of bladder cancer.

the results obtained in this study indicate that the combination of the M344 and the 19A211 antigenic markers in the immunocytology of exfoliated urothelial cells may improve the sensitivity of the detection of superficial bladder tumors.
the use of the monoclonal antibodies M344 and 19A211 for the detection of tumor‐associated antigens is of great potential value for the early detection and follow‐up of bladder cancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a number of tumor antigens and soluble molecules, which may provide useful diagnostic and prognostic information for patients with bladder cancer, and may also be useful for monitoring the effectiveness of chemopreventure measures.
we have developed a series of antigenic markers for bladder tumor subtypes and have identified a possible viral etiological factor for some of these tumors.
the use of monoclonal antibodies and PCR techniques has allowed us to identify new tumor antigens and to detect viral etiology of bladder cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no one-size-fits-all approach to cancer prevention.
the bladder is a good model for studying early and premalignan stages of tumors and for developing strategies of chemopreventions.
the bladder is a very good model for cancer chemoprevention.
